title: Set two light gates over an air track, straddling it, 200 mm apart
instruction: Set the two light gates over the air track for the speed run: each one straddling the track with both feet on the bench and nothing of it in the glider's path, square to the track, in front of the parked glider, the two gates 200 mm apart, centre to centre.
context: School and college science technicians set up the apparatus before each practical. For the speed and acceleration practicals (in England the GCSE and A-level required practicals, in US colleges the photogate labs), two light gates (photogates) go over an air track or runway: each straddles the track so that the card on the glider cuts its beam, square to the track, at the spacing the worksheet gives, with the glider's run left clear. A gate left resting on the track, or standing too close to it, stops the glider, and gates at the wrong spacing give every group the wrong speed. Here each gate is a free-standing inverted U that starts turned along the track: it must be lifted, turned square in the air and lowered so that its legs straddle the 30 mm track with 19 mm to spare on each side, then spaced from the other gate.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top (the lab bench) is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Air track: a fixed straight aluminium beam (silver), 30 mm wide (x), 440 mm long and 25 mm tall, centred at x 28.0 cm, y 0, running along y from y -22.0 to +22.0 cm. (2) End buffers: two fixed black rubber blocks, 40 mm (x) by 10 mm (y) and 35 mm tall, on the track's line against each end (centred at y +22.5 and -22.5 cm). (3) Glider, parked with the air off and fixed where it stands, blue plastic: a top plate 41 mm wide and 5 mm thick lying on the track's top (25 to 30 mm above the table); a side skirt 5 mm thick and 15 mm tall hanging beside each side of the track (10 to 25 mm up, 0.5 mm off it); all 70 mm long along y; and a black card 2 mm thick, 40 mm long and 25 mm tall standing on the plate's centre line (30 to 55 mm up; the card is what cuts a gate's beam). The glider is centred at x 28.0 cm, y +18.4 cm (from y +14.9 to +21.9 cm, 1 mm short of the left buffer); it runs toward -y. (4, 5) Two light gates, loose, black ABS, 80 g each, each an inverted U standing on two feet: two feet 12 mm (across the U) by 40 mm and 4 mm thick, centred 80 mm apart; on each foot a leg 10 x 20 mm and 70 mm tall (4 to 74 mm up); a crossbar 90 x 20 x 10 mm across the leg tops (74 to 84 mm up); and a red sensor window 10 x 10 mm, 1 mm proud, on the inner face of each leg, centred 45 mm up (the beam runs between the two windows). Overall 92 mm across, 40 mm deep and 84 mm tall, with 68 mm clear between the feet and between the windows and 74 mm under the crossbar: centred over the track, each foot is 19 mm from the track's side. The left gate stands on its feet centred at x 20.0 cm, y +26.0 cm, the right gate at x 20.0 cm, y -26.0 cm, both with the crossbar along y (turned along the track's direction, a quarter turn from square to it). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from where the two gates stand at the last step. A gate's 'centre' is the point midway between its feet; 'at rest' means neither foot moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. The glider's path is the space it sweeps on its run: within 22 mm of the track's centre line across the track (x 25.8 to 30.2 cm; the glider is 41 mm wide), from the table top up to 57 mm (the card's top is 55 mm), between the buffers (y -22.0 to +22.0 cm). A gate 'blocks the run' when any part of it (feet, legs, windows or crossbar, as it actually stands, turned or tilted; touching counts) is inside the path. A gate is 'set' when it is at rest with both feet flat on the table (every corner of each foot's underside within 3 mm of the table top), one foot on each side of the track, the crossbar within 10 degrees of square to the track seen from above (either way round), its centre between y -15.0 and +13.0 cm (the timing section: in front of the parked glider, the crossbar at least 9 mm clear of its front; and far enough from the far buffer that the glider, stopped against it, has carried its card right through the beam, the card's back edge 10 mm past the windows), and it does not block the run. Standing square, a gate clears the path with its centre up to 12 mm either side of the track's centre line; turned 10 degrees, up to 8 mm. Score 0 if either gate blocks the run (resting on the track, lying across it, or standing too close to it), whatever the other gate does. Otherwise: 0.25 for each set gate; when both are set, add 0.5 if their centres are 190 to 210 mm apart along the track (in y), or 0.25 if 180 to under 190 or over 210 to 220 mm apart. Possible scores: 0 (no gate set, or the run blocked), 0.25 (one gate set), 0.5 (both set, centres under 180 or over 220 mm apart), 0.75 (both set, 180 to under 190 or over 210 to 220 mm), 1.0 (both set, 190 to 210 mm); every outcome maps to exactly one. Either gate may be the nearer to the glider. A gate held above the table, standing beside the track, straddling the parked glider, a buffer or the last 7 cm before the far buffer, or turned more than 10 degrees from square is not set. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s. In a real trial, a top photo over a rule gives each gate's centre, its angle and the spacing, a 3 mm feeler gauge under each foot checks that it stands flat, and a card template 44 mm wide and 57 mm tall slid along the track from buffer to buffer checks that nothing is in the glider's path.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The track is shortened to 440 mm (real air tracks are 1 to 2 m long, triangular in section, with air holes) and is a plain box; the air is off and the glider fixed where parked. The beams are not simulated: the scorer checks where the gates stand, not a timer reading. Each gate is one rigid body of seven boxes (real ones are often clamped to a stand). The scorer sees only the gates, so a gate held still standing on the table counts as set.
reset_notes: Stand the left gate back on its feet centred at x 20.0 cm, y +26.0 cm and the right gate at x 20.0 cm, y -26.0 cm, both with the crossbar along y. The track, buffers and glider are fixed and do not move in the simulation; in a real trial, check that the glider is still parked against the left buffer (y +14.9 to +21.9 cm) and the track has not shifted. Nothing is consumed.
